newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM says to promote palladium short-covering.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM says to promote palladium short-covering.

text.p: The Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) said on Tuesday it will introduce a series of measures to make it easier for market participants to cover short positions in TOCOM palladium futures.
The measures will include expanded daily limits on price moves for all palladium futures contracts that currently trade with limits, a TOCOM official told reporters.
The September and October palladium contracts have ended with limit gains for a record seven consecutive sessions, the official said.

"We hope to introduce measures to encourage short-covering by market participants because the current market situation has left them unable to cover given current daily price limits," said Kazunari Hayakawa, a TOCOM general manager.
TOCOM will expand the daily price limits, effective on Wednesday, to 48 yen per gram from 36 yen per gram at present, he said.
The increase is in line with the New York Mercantile Exchange's (NYMEX) decision to raise its daily limit to $12 an ounce, he said.
He added that TOCOM will also raise margins on all palladium contracts by 27,000 yen, effective on Wednesday.
